transcript.text: Alright, let's get the capacity review started. We need to finalize the production capacity policy for the image-processing pipeline before the seasonal traffic increase hits. The current draft has 12 baseline workers, scales out at 100 queued jobs, uses any available processing region, and puts all customers in a single FIFO queue. Before I can approve anything, I need to hear from FinOps, SRE, security, and customer support on operational requirements. Who wants to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While I was reconciling this month's cloud invoice for another service, I confirmed that the available compute reservation applies to this pipeline only with exactly 18 baseline workers and a monthly capacity ceiling of exactly $24,000. The draft's 12-worker plan has no reservation commitment, and I haven't yet updated the capacity proposal to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something from a load investigation I ran this morning. During a separate burst-pattern test, I measured an 11-minute worker startup time. The pipeline needs exactly 6 warm workers with scale-out triggered at exactly 40 queued jobs to keep processing latency within our operating target. I have not yet filed this result in the capacity review.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a security constraint I found during an unrelated access review of the image-processing deployment manifest. Customer-uploaded image data must run in exactly eu-central-1 and must use the tenant-managed KMS key named tenant_kms. The current draft permits any processing region and doesn't specify that key, so it would violate this requirement. I haven't opened the security finding formally yet, but this needs to be corrected before the policy can be approved.

transcript.text: I need to share a customer support finding from a recent escalation. Lumen Media's production workflow requires their image jobs to use a dedicated priority queue rather than the shared FIFO queue. The current draft puts all customers in one FIFO queue, which would not meet this customer's operational requirement. I have not yet added this to the capacity proposal, but it needs to be addressed before the policy is approved.
transcript.speaker: A5
